derivations.claim:
For each $n\ge1$, iterate the product-tensor unitary of [F2]; induction
on $n$ gives a unitary from $H^{\widehat\otimes n}$ to the full completed
product $L^2(X^n)$. On elementary tensors the permutation $U_\pi$ becomes
coordinate permutation, so by density the unitary intertwines $P_{s,n}$ with
averaging over coordinate permutations [F3]. Its restriction identifies
$H_s^{(n)}$ with the closed symmetric subspace. The $n=0$ sector is $\mathbb C$
by definition. Each $s_n$ is measurable as a finite sum of measurable
coordinate maps and is invariant under all permutations.

Let $\Omega=\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}X^n$ be the countable disjoint union, with the completed product measure on each component and unit mass on $X^0$; write $s_j$ for $s_{n,j}$ on component $n$. The Fock realization in step 1.1 is a closed subspace of $L^2(\Omega)$ consisting of symmetric components. Define $E(B)$ by multiplication by $\mathbf1_{s^{-1}(B)}$. Since $s$ is invariant under permutations, this multiplier preserves the symmetric subspace. It is an orthogonal projection because its multiplier is real and idempotent; $E(\varnothing)=0$, $E(\mathbb R^d)=I$ and $E(B)E(C)=E(B\cap C)$ follow pointwise. For disjoint $B_k$ with union $B$, the squared norm of $E(B)\Psi-\sum_{k=0}^N E(B_k)\Psi$ is $$\sum_{n\ge0}\int_{X^n} \mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B\setminus\cup_{k=0}^N B_k)}|\Psi_n|^2\,d\mu_n.$$ The indicators tend pointwise to zero and the integrand is bounded by $|\Psi_n|^2$, whose total integral is $\|\Psi\|^2$; dominated convergence [F6] gives norm convergence. Hence $E$ is a strongly countably additive PVM.

Fix a real measurable multiplier $f$ on $\Omega$ that is invariant under coordinate permutations, and define $M_f\Psi=f\Psi$ on the symmetric domain $D(M_f)=\{\Psi:f\Psi\in L^2(\Omega)\}$. This domain is dense: the symmetric cutoffs $\Psi\mathbf1_{|f|\le m}$ belong to it and converge in norm by dominated convergence. Reality of $f$ makes $M_f$ symmetric. If $\Psi\in D(M_f^*)$ and $K=M_f^*\Psi$, then for each $m$ the vector $v_m=(f\Psi-K)\mathbf1_{|f|\le m}$ is symmetric and lies in $D(M_f)$, since $f$ is bounded on its support. The adjoint identity gives $$0=\langle M_fv_m,\Psi\rangle_2-\langle v_m,K\rangle_2 =\int_{|f|\le m}|f\Psi-K|^2\,d\mu_\Omega.$$ Taking the union over $m$ shows $f\Psi=K$ almost everywhere, so $\Psi\in D(M_f)$ and $M_f^*\Psi=M_f\Psi$. Conversely, for every $\Psi\in D(M_f)$, reality of $f$ gives the adjoint identity against every domain vector, so $M_f^*\Psi=M_f\Psi$. Therefore $M_f$ is self-adjoint on its maximal multiplication domain. Apply this to $f=s_j$ to obtain each self-adjoint $H_j$, and to $f=\theta\cdot s$ to obtain $H_\theta$.

For each $j$, the multiplier $s_j$ defines $H_j$ with the displayed component domain because the squared norm of $H_j\Psi$ is exactly $\sum_n\int|s_{n,j}|^2|\Psi_n|^2d\mu_n$; the vacuum term is zero. For $\theta$, the same calculation gives $D(H_\theta)=\{\Psi:\sum_n\int|\theta\cdot s_n|^2|\Psi_n|^2d\mu_n<\infty\}$. The PVM from step 2.1 has coordinate functions $s_j$, so its indicators give the joint spectral projections for all the $H_j$ and its scalar-coordinate multipliers have these exact domains. Truncating a vector in any such domain after sector $N$ makes both its norm tail and operator-image tail tend to zero; hence $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_j)$ and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_\theta)$ are graph cores.

By [F6], $U_\theta(t)$ is unitary and $U_\theta(t+s)=U_\theta(t)U_\theta(s)$ on each component, including the vacuum where the phase is one. For any $\Psi$, the squared norm of $U_\theta(t)\Psi-U_\theta(t_0)\Psi$ is the integral over $\Omega$ of $|e^{it\theta\cdot s}-e^{it_0\theta\cdot s}|^2|\Psi|^2$; the integrand tends pointwise to zero and is bounded by $4|\Psi|^2$, so [F6] proves strong continuity. If $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$, the pointwise difference quotient tends to $i(\theta\cdot s)\Psi$ and its squared error is bounded by $4|\theta\cdot s|^2|\Psi|^2$; dominated convergence proves norm convergence. Conversely, if the difference quotient has a norm limit as $t\to0$, take $t_m=1/m$. Fatou's lemma [F6] on the disjoint union gives $$\sum_n\int|\theta\cdot s_n|^2|\Psi_n|^2d\mu_n \le\liminf_m\left\|\frac{U_\theta(t_m)\Psi-\Psi}{t_m}\right\|^2<\infty,$$ so $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$; the forward calculation identifies the limit as $iH_\theta\Psi$. This proves the exact derivative criterion and all claims.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space and let
$\boldsymbol\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d):X\to\mathbb R^d$ be a
finite-valued measurable map, where $d\ge1$. Put
$H=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ with the second-variable-linear pairing of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and form the bosonic Fock space
$\mathcal F_s(H)$. For $n\ge1$, identify $H_s^{(n)}$ with the symmetric
subspace of $L^2(X^n,\overline{\mu^{\times n}};\mathbb C)$ by iterating
[[lem-qft-l2-product-tensor-identification]]. Set $X^0=\{\star\}$,
$s_0(\star)=0$, and for $n\ge1$ set
$$s_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{r=1}^n\boldsymbol\omega(x_r)\in\mathbb R^d.$$
For $1\le j\le d$, define $H_j$ by multiplication by the $j$th coordinate
$s_{n,j}$ on sector $n$, with exact domain
$$D(H_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n): \sum_{n\ge1}\int_{X^n}|s_{n,j}|^2|\Psi_n|^2\,d\overline{\mu^{\times n}}<\infty\right\}.$$
Each $H_j$ is self-adjoint, and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_j)$ is a
graph core. The joint projection-valued measure
[[def-projection-valued-measure]] on $\mathbb R^d$ is
$$(E(B)\Psi)_n=\mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B)}\Psi_n\quad(n\ge1),\qquad (E(B)\Psi)_0=\mathbf1_B(0)\Psi_0.$$
For $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, let $H_\theta$ be multiplication on sector $n$
by $\theta\cdot s_n$, with its maximal square-integrability domain. Then
$$U_\theta(t)\Psi:=\bigl(e^{it\theta\cdot s_n}\Psi_n\bigr)_{n\ge0}$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on all of Fock space, and its norm
derivative at zero exists exactly for $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$, where it is
$iH_\theta\Psi$. The zero-particle sector is the vacuum eigenvector at joint
value $0$.
